name: Warm Enough
tagline: Heat the home you have for less, without the damp
about: Warm Enough builds a heating schedule for your routine, finds draughts from a photo, balances and bleeds radiators, compares the real cost of heaters and keeps damp and mould away when you heat less.
persona: You are a heating engineer turned energy adviser: numbers on degrees and kilowatt-hours, no gadget-selling, and firm about carbon monoxide and mould safety.

onboarding.title: Warm rooms, smaller bills
onboarding.subtitle: Your heating type and home shape every number.
bullets: A schedule that fits your day

tools.title: Heating schedule
tools.subtitle: Thermostat times for your real week

inputs.label: Weekly routine
inputs.placeholder: out 8–6 weekdays, home all weekend, baby naps 1–3

tools.prompt: Design a heating schedule for the profile heating around: {routine}, targeting {temp}°C when home. Table (Period | Weekdays | Weekends | Setpoint | Why), kv (estimated % saving versus constant heating, setback temperature, warm-up lead time for the profile heating type), bullets on room-by-room tweaks (TRVs, closing doors), and a callout on the minimum safe temperature for pipes, damp and vulnerable people.

tools.title: Draught detective
tools.subtitle: Photo of a window, door or floor → fixes

inputs.label: Photo of the suspect window, door or gap
Where and what you feel
inputs.placeholder: bedroom sash window, cold air at the bottom

tools.prompt: From the photo and '{where}': table (Gap found | Likely cause | Fix | Cost | DIY minutes), steps for the cheapest effective fix in order, a checklist for a whole-home draught hunt (candle or incense test, letterbox, loft hatch, floorboards, chimney), and a callout on ventilation you must NOT block (trickle vents, extractor fans, gas-appliance vents).

tools.title: Radiators & controls
tools.subtitle: Bleed, balance, TRVs, boiler flow
tools.prompt: Fix '{issue}' for the profile heating: text on the cause, steps with tool names (bleed key, lockshield spanner) and safety notes, a table (Room type | TRV setting | Target °C), kv (suggested boiler flow temperature and expected saving if it's a combi or condensing boiler), and a callout on what needs a Gas Safe or licensed engineer.

tools.title: Heater cost per hour
tools.subtitle: Which heater, and heat the person or the room?

inputs.label: Options you're weighing
inputs.placeholder: 2kW fan heater, oil radiator, heated throw, just the gas central heating

tools.prompt: Compare: {options} for {hours} hours a day at the profile tariff: table (Option | kW | Cost per hour | Cost per month | Best for), kv (cheapest for one person at a desk, cheapest for a whole room, safest overnight), bullets on 'heat the person' tricks that work, and a callout on heater safety (unattended use, extension leads, drying clothes on them).

tools.title: Damp & mould when heating less
tools.subtitle: Condensation, ventilation, humidity

inputs.label: What you're seeing
inputs.placeholder: black spots on bedroom ceiling corners, wet windows every morning

tools.prompt: For: {signs} — text on the cause (condensation versus penetrating versus rising damp), steps for a daily routine of heating, ventilation and humidity control with a target humidity %, a table (Room | Moisture source | Fix | Cost), a checklist for safe mould cleaning, and a callout on health risks and when to involve a landlord or surveyor.

disclaimer: General guidance only; gas, flue and electrical work needs a qualified engineer, fit carbon-monoxide alarms, and never block ventilation for fuel-burning appliances.
